derivation.method: hybrid: power-law bathymetry below DSM water surface + DEM hypsometry above
derivation.base_elevation_source: DEM riverbed at the dam toe
derivation.caveat: Bathymetry below the DSM water surface is RECONSTRUCTED, not surveyed. It is constrained by the published gross storage and the satellite-observed surface area. Replace with a bathymetric survey where one exists.

peak_discharge_envelopes.interpretation: Routed peak lies outside the published envelopes, but this reservoir is outside the range those regressions were fitted to (<~1 km3, <~100 m head), so the physically routed value is the primary estimate and the envelopes are context only.

model_comparison.description: 2D shallow-water (Delft3D-FM class) driven by the empirical breach weir hydrograph

hazard.hazard_rating_note: Defra FD2321 was calibrated for depths of a few metres and velocities of a few m/s. Beyond class 4 ('dangerous for all') the number carries no extra meaning, so it is clipped for reporting; the raw maximum is given alongside.

classes.name: Extreme
classes.description: Dangerous for all, including emergency services

buildings.damage_curve: JRC Huizinga et al. (2017), Asia residential

unit_values_used._provenance: USER-SUPPLIED ASSUMPTION - not measured data. Replace with audited schedule-of-rates for the study area.

losses.caveat: Monetary figures are derived from the unit rates above, which are assumptions, not measurements. Physical exposure counts are from OSM/WorldPop/WorldCover and are the defensible output.

warnings: 31,474 people exposed against only 6 inundated OSM buildings (5,246 people per mapped building). OSM building coverage is sparse in this area, so the building count is a lower bound and damage-to-buildings is understated.

notes: CONTEXT ONLY - not a skill score. The dam-break scenario is hypothetical, so no satellite image of it exists. The SAR scene shows the pre-event water body; the difference is the land the scenario would newly inundate.

basemap.description: Sentinel-2 true colour, relief-shaded, with DEM hillshade filling granule gaps
